pageInfo.subtitle: Protect tendons, expand finger span, prevent repetitive strain injury (RSI), and prepare your arms for peak guitar performance.
pageInfo.heroDescription: Your hands, wrists, forearms, and shoulders are the physical biomechanical engine that drives your music. Professional musicians treat their bodies with the same rigorous care as Olympic athletes. Diving into intense, high-speed guitar practice with cold, stiff muscles is the fastest route to carpal tunnel syndrome, flexor tendinitis, and debilitating focal dystonia. This masterclass delivers physical-therapy-backed tendon-gliding routines, wrist decompression stretches, and progressive on-instrument reach drills that safeguard your hands for decades of injury-free playing.

guidelines.title: The Physiology of Hand Health & Injury Prevention

items.text: Warm Tissue Before Stretching: Never perform aggressive static stretches on ice-cold hands. Spend 2–3 minutes shaking out hands, doing gentle air circles, or washing hands in warm water first.
The Pain-Free Threshold: You should feel gentle tension in the muscle belly—never sharp, burning, or tingling sensations in the wrist or joints. Pain is your nervous system's emergency stop signal.
Sustained Holds Without Bouncing: Hold static stretches smoothly for 15 to 30 seconds. Bouncing activates the muscle spindle reflex, causing fibers to contract and tighten instead of lengthening.

Diaphragmatic Breathing: Inhale deeply through the nose and exhale slowly through the mouth while holding each stretch. Slow breathing downregulates the sympathetic nervous system, releasing systemic tension.
Tendon-Gliding Sequences: Move your fingers through five fundamental shapes (Straight, Hook, Fist, Tabletop, Flat Fist) to ensure flexor tendons glide smoothly through the carpal tunnel.
Neutral Wrist Angle: Keep your fretting wrist as straight as possible (less than a 15-degree bend). Extreme wrist flexion or extension constricts the carpal tunnel, leading to numbness.

Optimal Guitar Strap Height: Position your guitar at the same torso height when sitting and standing. Slumping the guitar down to your knees forces the fretting wrist into a severe, injury-causing angle.
The 25-Minute Reset Rule: Set a timer for 25 minutes. When it sounds, put the guitar on its stand for 3 minutes, shake out your arms, roll your shoulders, and hydrate.

Cervical Spine Awareness: Avoid hunching over the fretboard with your neck craned forward ('text neck'). Keep your ears aligned over your shoulders and glance down with your eyes rather than dropping your head.
Forearm Self-Myofascial Release: Gently massage the flexor and extensor muscles along your forearm using the opposite thumb or a massage ball to break up micro-adhesions.

exercises.title: Wrist Extensor & Flexor Stretches (Prayer & Reverse)
exercises.description: The foundational stretches for every instrumentalist. Extend one arm forward with elbow straight, palm facing away, and gently draw the fingers backward with the opposite hand (extensor stretch). Hold 20 seconds. Then point fingers down and press gently toward the forearm (flexor stretch).

patternNote.text: Protocol: 20-second holds each side (Extensors & Flexors) with relaxed shoulders

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Never pull aggressively on the fingers. Apply gentle, progressive pressure. You should feel a soothing stretch across the underside and top of your forearm.

exercises.title: The 5-Stage Tendon-Gliding Sequence
exercises.description: The gold-standard hand therapy exercise developed to lubricate and mobilize the flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus tendons through the carpal sheath: (1) Straight hand, (2) Hook fist (claws), (3) Full fist, (4) Tabletop (knuckles bent, fingers straight), (5) Straight fist.

patternNote.text: 5 Stages: Straight -> Hook Fist -> Full Fist -> Tabletop -> Straight Fist (5 reps)

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Perform 5 complete cycles with each hand. Hold each position for 3 seconds. This flushes synovial fluid across the tendon sheaths, instantly reducing internal friction.

exercises.title: Interdigital Web-Space & Finger Spread Stretches
exercises.description: Increase your physical reach for wide chord voicings and 3NPS scale runs by gently opening the interdigital web spaces between fingers 1-2, 2-3, and 3-4 using your opposite hand or your guitar neck.

patternNote.text: Target: Web spaces between 1-2, 2-3, and 3-4 (10 seconds per finger gap)

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Gently separate adjacent fingers sideways. Do not force the fingers apart. Over weeks, this increases the elasticity of the palmar fascia, adding up to half an inch of natural reach.

exercises.title: Cervical Spine, Shoulder & Scapular Decompression
exercises.description: Counteract guitar posture syndrome. Perform 10 large backward shoulder rolls, followed by gentle neck lateral flexion (tilting ear to shoulder, holding 15 seconds each side), and chin tucks to decompress the cervical vertebrae.

patternNote.text: Decompression: Shoulder rolls (10 reps) + Lateral neck tilts (15 sec each)

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: All nerves controlling your fingers originate in the cervical spine (C5–T1). Releasing neck and shoulder tension directly restores blood flow and nerve conduction to your hands.

exercises.title: Gentle Micro-Pressure Activation (Frets 5 to 8)
exercises.description: Transition to the guitar gently. Position your fingers at frets 5 through 8 (where fret spacing is narrower than at the nut). Press each fret with absolute minimal pressure—just enough to sound a clean note—across all 6 strings.

patternNote.text: Frets: 5, 6, 7, 8 ascending across all 6 strings at slow 60 BPM

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Focus on relaxation. Consciously relax your jaw, drop your shoulders, and feel the gentle curve of your fingers. Press with feather-light touch right behind the fretwire.

exercises.title: Progressive Fret-Span Expansion (2 to 5 Fret Reach)
exercises.description: Systematically expand your physical finger span on the guitar. Anchor finger 1 on fret 5, and progressively stretch fingers 2, 3, and 4 to frets 6, 7, 8, and 9 on the G and B strings.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: When reaching for fret 9 with your pinky, slightly lower your fretting thumb behind the neck to allow your hand to spread naturally like a fan. Stop if you feel joint strain.

exercises.title: The Allan Holdsworth Wide-Interval Finger Stretch Etude
exercises.description: Inspired by Allan Holdsworth's legendary reach. Spans frets 5, 7, 9, and 10 across strings 4 through 1 with effortless legato, demonstrating how neutral wrist posture unlocks massive reach without physical pain.

patternNote.text: Master Reach: 6-fret diatonic stretch across strings 4 to 1

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice how dropping your wrist into a completely neutral position—with the neck tilted up at a 45-degree angle—allows your pinky to reach the 10th fret without strain.

tips.title: Preserving Your Hands for a Lifetime

items.title: 3 Dangerous Habits That Cause Guitar Injuries
items: The 'No Pain, No Gain' Fallacy: Pushing through tingling, numbness, or sharp pain. Tendons and nerves do not adapt like muscles; pain signals microscopic damage that requires immediate rest.
The Slung-Low Guitar Strap: Wearing your guitar around your knees for rock swagger forces your fretting wrist into a severe 90-degree bend, triggering carpal tunnel compression.
Cold-Room Shredding: Playing high-speed solos immediately after entering a cold room. Cold tendons are brittle; warm your hands thoroughly before touching the instrument.

items.title: Performing Arts Medicine & Hand Science
items: Dr. Alice Brandfonbrener: Founder of the Medical Problems of Performing Artists journal; proved that 80% of musician overuse injuries stem from inadequate warmups and sudden practice spikes.
John Petrucci: Dream Theater virtuoso who credits his 40-year injury-free shred career to strict pre-practice forearm stretches, warm water soaks, and regular practice breaks.
Allan Holdsworth: Famously possessed massive reach not from oversized hands, but from perfect classical posture and complete absence of muscular antagonism.
The Alexander Technique: Classical conservatory method focusing on releasing head, neck, and shoulder compression to restore natural arm freedom.

items.title: The 10-Minute Daily Hand Health Routine
items: Block 1: Warm Tissue & Wrist Stretches (3 min) - Warm hands with warm water or friction, then perform 20-second holds of wrist extensor and flexor stretches.
Block 2: 5-Stage Tendon-Gliding Sequence (3 min) - Complete 5 cycles of tendon glides to lubricate the carpal sheath and web spaces.
Block 3: On-Instrument Micro-Pressure & Reach (4 min) - Run Exercises 5 & 6 at 60 BPM with feather-light touch before starting your main practice.
